title: Deep Learning / LLM Foundations — universal-기초 concept dictionary
name: ml-foundations
summary: Concise reference of the timeless, textbook mechanisms shared by all modern deep-learning models and LLMs (learning-mechanics · architecture-primitives · training-paradigms · numerics-and-inference). This is the universal base layer that frontier-models.json (per-lab tricks) builds on; entries are general mechanisms, not vendor-specific.
note: reference primer for ARCHITECTURE.json ingestion; standard textbook concepts, timeless

children.name: 역전파(backpropagation)
children.summary: 역전파(backpropagation): reverse-mode automatic differentiation applying the chain rule backward through the computation graph to compute every parameter's gradient in one pass — the engine of all neural-net training.

children.name: forward/backward pass
children.summary: forward/backward pass: forward computes outputs+loss layer-by-layer caching activations; backward propagates gradients from loss to inputs reusing those caches — one training step is forward then backward then update.

children.name: computational graph
children.summary: computational graph: a DAG of tensor ops (nodes) and data dependencies (edges) that autodiff traverses; static (compiled) or dynamic (define-by-run) graphs enable automatic gradient computation and op fusion.

children.name: 경사하강법(gradient descent / SGD)
children.summary: 경사하강법(gradient descent): iteratively step parameters opposite the loss gradient; SGD uses noisy mini-batch gradients, trading exactness for speed and an implicit regularizing noise that aids generalization.

children.name: momentum & Nesterov
children.summary: momentum: accumulate an exponentially-decayed velocity of past gradients to dampen oscillation and accelerate down ravines; Nesterov evaluates the gradient at the look-ahead point for a more responsive correction.

children.name: Adam / AdamW
children.summary: Adam: per-parameter adaptive LR from running 1st+2nd gradient moments; AdamW decouples weight decay from the adaptive step, fixing Adam's broken L2 and becoming the default LLM optimizer.

children.name: RMSprop / Adagrad
children.summary: RMSprop/Adagrad: scale each parameter's step by a running average of squared gradients so rare/large-gradient directions get smaller steps; Adagrad's sum monotonically shrinks LR, RMSprop's decay keeps it alive.

children.name: Adafactor
children.summary: Adafactor: memory-frugal Adam variant that factorizes the second-moment matrix into row/column statistics instead of storing it per-parameter, enabling large-model training under tight optimizer-state memory.

children.name: Muon
children.summary: Muon: a recent optimizer that orthogonalizes momentum updates for 2D weight matrices (via Newton–Schulz iteration), reported to improve token-efficiency on large LM pretraining versus AdamW.

children.name: learning-rate schedules
children.summary: LR schedules: vary step size over training — linear warmup ramps LR from ~0 to stabilize early unstable updates, then cosine/linear decay anneals toward 0 for a sharper final minimum.

children.name: loss functions
children.summary: loss functions: cross-entropy for classification/next-token (matches softmax, penalizes confident errors), MSE for regression, contrastive/InfoNCE pulls matched pairs together and pushes negatives apart.

children.name: vanishing/exploding gradients
children.summary: vanishing/exploding gradients: in deep/recurrent nets repeated Jacobian multiplication shrinks gradients to ~0 (no learning) or blows them up (instability); mitigated by residuals, normalization, init, and gating.

children.name: gradient clipping
children.summary: gradient clipping: cap the global gradient norm (or value) before the update so rare large gradients can't destabilize training — a cheap standard guard for exploding gradients in transformers and RNNs.

children.name: artificial neuron / MLP
children.summary: neuron/MLP: a neuron computes a weighted sum + bias through a nonlinearity; stacking fully-connected layers forms a multilayer perceptron, a universal function approximator and the transformer's FFN building block.

children.name: activation functions
children.summary: activations: nonlinearities that let nets model nonlinear maps — ReLU (cheap, sparse), GELU (smooth, transformer default), sigmoid/tanh (bounded, gate signals), SwiGLU (gated FFN boosting LLM quality).

children.name: softmax
children.summary: softmax: exponentiate-and-normalize a vector into a probability distribution; turns logits into class/token probabilities and forms attention weights, with temperature controlling sharpness.

children.name: 어텐션(scaled dot-product attention)
children.summary: 어텐션(attention): each query scores all keys via dot product scaled by 1/√d, softmaxes into weights, and returns a weighted sum of values — content-based routing that lets any token read from any other.

children.name: self vs cross attention
children.summary: self vs cross attention: self-attention has Q,K,V from the same sequence (modeling internal dependencies); cross-attention draws Q from one sequence and K,V from another (e.g. decoder attending to encoder).

children.name: multi-head attention (MHA)
children.summary: multi-head attention: run several attention heads in parallel on learned low-dim projections and concatenate, letting the model attend to different relationships/subspaces simultaneously.

children.name: MQA / GQA
children.summary: MQA/GQA: share K,V across heads to shrink the KV-cache — Multi-Query uses one K,V for all heads, Grouped-Query shares within head-groups, trading a little quality for big inference-memory/bandwidth savings.

children.name: KV-cache
children.summary: KV-cache: store past tokens' keys/values during autoregressive decoding so each new token attends without recomputing them — turns generation from O(n²) per step into O(n), at the cost of growing memory.

children.name: FlashAttention
children.summary: FlashAttention: IO-aware exact-attention kernel that tiles Q,K,V through fast SRAM and never materializes the full n×n score matrix, giving large speedups and linear memory in sequence length.

children.name: linear/sparse attention
children.summary: linear/sparse attention: approximate or restrict full attention to beat its O(n²) cost — sparse patterns (windowed/strided/global) or kernel linearizations trade some global reach for long-context scalability.

children.name: Transformer block & residual connections
children.summary: transformer block: stacked (attention + position-wise FFN) sublayers each wrapped with a residual skip connection so gradients flow and the block learns a refinement on top of identity.

children.name: LayerNorm vs RMSNorm
children.summary: LayerNorm vs RMSNorm: LayerNorm re-centers and re-scales activations per token (mean+variance); RMSNorm drops the mean step and normalizes by root-mean-square only — cheaper and now common in LLMs.

children.name: pre-norm vs post-norm
children.summary: pre-norm vs post-norm: post-norm (original) normalizes after the residual add; pre-norm normalizes inside the residual branch, giving much more stable gradients and enabling very deep transformer training.

children.name: FFN (feed-forward network)
children.summary: FFN: the per-token MLP in each transformer block (up-project → nonlinearity → down-project, typically 4×width); holds most parameters and acts as the model's key-value associative memory.

children.name: positional encoding
children.summary: positional encoding: inject token-order into permutation-invariant attention — fixed sinusoidal, learned embeddings, RoPE (rotate Q/K by position for relative encoding), or ALiBi (linear distance bias on scores).

children.name: embeddings & embedding matrix
children.summary: embeddings: a lookup matrix maps each token id to a dense vector the model operates on; tied embeddings reuse this matrix as the output projection, saving parameters and coupling input/output token spaces.

children.name: tokenization (BPE)
children.summary: tokenization: split text into subword units so a fixed vocabulary covers any string; Byte-Pair Encoding (and byte-level BPE) greedily merges frequent pairs, balancing vocab size against sequence length.

children.name: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
children.summary: MoE: replace the FFN with many expert sub-networks plus a router that top-k-gates each token to a few experts, scaling total parameters while keeping per-token compute (active params) low.

children.name: MoE routing & load balancing
children.summary: MoE routing: the gating network picks experts per token; an auxiliary load-balancing loss (or aux-free bias) spreads tokens evenly so no expert is starved or overloaded and capacity isn't wasted.

children.name: convolution (CNN)
children.summary: convolution: slide shared learnable kernels over spatial input to extract translation-equivariant local features with weight sharing — the dominant vision primitive pre-transformers and still common in hybrids.

children.name: RNN / LSTM / GRU
children.summary: RNN/LSTM: process sequences step-by-step through a recurrent hidden state; LSTM/GRU add gates to carry long-range information past vanishing gradients — the pre-transformer sequence model, now mostly historical.

children.name: pretraining (causal/masked LM)
children.summary: pretraining: self-supervised learning on raw text — causal LM predicts the next token left-to-right (GPT-style), masked LM predicts held-out tokens from both sides (BERT-style); builds general representations cheaply.

children.name: fine-tuning (full)
children.summary: full fine-tuning: continue training all weights of a pretrained model on a downstream task/dataset — maximally expressive but costly in compute and storage and prone to overwriting general knowledge.

children.name: PEFT: LoRA / QLoRA / adapters
children.summary: PEFT: adapt a frozen model by training few extra params — LoRA injects low-rank ΔW matrices, QLoRA does LoRA over a 4-bit-quantized base, adapters insert small bottleneck layers; cheap, swappable, memory-light.

children.name: instruction tuning
children.summary: instruction tuning: supervised fine-tuning on (instruction, response) pairs so a base model follows natural-language commands and adopts a helpful assistant format — the SFT stage before preference alignment.

children.name: RLHF
children.summary: RLHF: align a model to human preferences — train a reward model from comparison data, then optimize the policy against it (often with PPO) under a KL penalty to stay near the reference model.

children.name: reward model
children.summary: reward model: a model trained on human (or AI) preference comparisons to score outputs, providing the scalar signal that RLHF/PPO optimizes — the learned proxy for 'what humans prefer'.

children.name: PPO
children.summary: PPO: the policy-gradient RL algorithm typical in RLHF; a clipped surrogate objective limits how far each update moves the policy, keeping training stable while maximizing the reward model's score.

children.name: DPO
children.summary: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization): skip the explicit reward model and RL loop by optimizing a closed-form classification loss directly on preference pairs — simpler and more stable than PPO-based RLHF.

children.name: GRPO
children.summary: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization): a critic-free RL method that estimates advantage from the mean reward of a sampled group of responses, cutting memory vs PPO; popular for reasoning/RLVR training.

children.name: KL penalty
children.summary: KL penalty: a divergence term keeping the trained policy close to the reference (SFT) model during RL, preventing reward-hacking and degeneration while still letting it improve on the reward signal.

children.name: knowledge distillation
children.summary: knowledge distillation: train a small student to mimic a large teacher's soft output distribution (and/or hidden states), transferring capability into a cheaper model that learns from richer-than-hard-label signal.

children.name: curriculum learning
children.summary: curriculum learning: order training data from easy to hard (or by quality/length) so the model builds foundations before difficult examples, often improving convergence speed and final quality.

children.name: data mixing
children.summary: data mixing: choose the proportions of corpora/domains (web, code, math, books) in the training mixture; weights strongly shape capabilities and are tuned, sometimes annealed, for the target skill profile.

children.name: catastrophic forgetting
children.summary: catastrophic forgetting: fine-tuning on new data erodes previously learned abilities as weights overwrite; countered by data replay, PEFT, regularization, or rehearsal to preserve old knowledge.

children.name: scaling laws (Chinchilla)
children.summary: scaling laws: loss falls as a smooth power law in params N, data D, and compute C; Chinchilla shows compute-optimal training scales D and N together (~20 tokens per parameter), favoring more data over sheer size.

children.name: mixed precision (FP16/BF16/FP8/FP4)
children.summary: mixed precision: compute in low precision (FP16/BF16, increasingly FP8/FP4) while keeping a master FP32 copy and loss-scaling, slashing memory+bandwidth and speeding tensor-core matmuls with little accuracy loss.

children.name: quantization (PTQ / QAT)
children.summary: quantization: represent weights/activations in low-bit ints/floats to shrink and accelerate models — PTQ calibrates an already-trained model, quantization-aware training (QAT) simulates it during training for accuracy.

children.name: GPTQ / AWQ
children.summary: GPTQ/AWQ: weight-only PTQ for LLMs — GPTQ minimizes per-layer reconstruction error via second-order updates, AWQ scales activation-salient weights before rounding; both give ~4-bit inference with minimal quality drop.

children.name: GGUF k-quants
children.summary: GGUF k-quants: the llama.cpp file format and block-wise mixed-bit quantization schemes (Q4_K, Q5_K, …) that allocate more bits to sensitive weights, enabling efficient CPU/consumer-GPU local inference.

children.name: sampling/decoding
children.summary: decoding: choose the next token from the output distribution — greedy/argmax (deterministic), temperature (rescale randomness), top-k (k likeliest), top-p/nucleus (smallest mass-p set), balancing quality vs diversity.

children.name: beam search
children.summary: beam search: keep the top-B partial sequences by cumulative log-prob at each step, exploring multiple hypotheses for higher-likelihood outputs; strong for translation but tends to bland text in open-ended generation.

children.name: speculative decoding
children.summary: speculative decoding: a cheap draft model proposes several tokens that the big model verifies in one parallel pass, accepting the matching prefix — lossless speedup that exploits spare compute to cut latency.

children.name: continuous batching
children.summary: continuous/in-flight batching: serving scheduler that adds and evicts requests at the token level instead of waiting for a whole batch, keeping the GPU saturated and maximizing throughput under mixed-length traffic.

children.name: bias-variance tradeoff
children.summary: bias-variance tradeoff: error decomposes into bias (underfitting, too-simple model) and variance (overfitting, too data-sensitive); generalization comes from balancing the two via capacity and regularization.

children.name: regularization
children.summary: regularization: techniques to curb overfitting — dropout randomly zeros activations, weight decay penalizes large weights, label smoothing softens targets, early stopping halts at best validation loss.
